about: F8. What a player would say they saw, mapped to the mechanics that could produce it.
Read `player` as the sentence someone says at the table. Read `candidates` as every
mechanic that could have caused it, each with p = how strongly that mechanic implies
this observation. A symptom with one candidate is usually a symptom written lazily:
the whole point is that observations are ambiguous and the ontology should say so.
Matchers, all optional and ANDed within a candidate:
traitTag / actionTag  5e.tools' own curated label. Exact, near-certain, ~50 exist.
text                  regex over an entry's name + body. Case-insensitive, dotAll.
name                  regex over an entry's name only.
unless                regex that vetoes a text/name hit on the same entry.
where                 restrict to entry kinds: trait, action, bonus, reaction,
legendary, spellcasting, defence. Default is all of them.
`mechanics` is every kind EXCEPT defence, and any symptom about
an effect the monster INFLICTS wants it: 'inflicts frightened'
and 'cannot be frightened' share a word, so scanning the defence
block for one matches every creature with the other.
field                 structural predicate on the statblock, e.g. speed.burrow,
sense.tremorsense, condimmune.charmed, immune.fire,
dealsdamage.psychic, type.undead, size.huge, lair, legendary,
spellcasting, language.common, reach.15
`volatile` marks a symptom whose underlying mechanic GMs add and remove freely, so a
party reporting it is weak evidence AGAINST a candidate that lacks it. Legendary and
lair actions are the case the handoff names: promoting an ordinary monster to a boss is
one of the commonest things a GM does, and the observation is true of the fight without
being true of the statblock. Credit is unchanged; only the miss penalty is discounted.

`collectedBy` names another module that asks for this observation better, and removes the symptom from the "what did it do?" list. The ten damage-type symptoms are all "it burned me" and its siblings; an attack row asks the same question paired to a single action, which is strictly stronger evidence. The symptom stays here because the tagger still uses it to index the corpus — only the player-facing list drops it.
`testable` marks a symptom the party can deliberately provoke in about one round.
F13 prefers those when it suggests a discriminating test — 'hit it with radiant' is
advice; 'wait to see if it rejuvenates in a few days' is not.
This file is expected to grow forever. Adding a symptom is a data edit, never a code
edit — that is the whole reason it lives out here.
